units.translation: He has a newly made, well-fitted shield.
An altar is stronger than a tower, an unbreakable shield.
Scholium: τῷ πληρωτή [to the filler], παρὰ τὸ σάσσω [from the verb 'to stuff'], ὅτι δι᾽ αὐτὸν ἀπέθανεν [because he died on account of him].
the youth slain by Xerxes, the stuffer of Hades with Persians.
to the filler, from the verb 'to stuff', because he died on account of him

Etym. M. p. 151, 49. ἀσαλής [carefree]: ἡ ἄφροντις [the one without care], ἡ μηδενός φροντίζουσα [the one who thinks about nothing]. σάλη γὰρ ἡ φροντίς [for σάλη is care]. ἀσαλὴς ὁ ἀμέριμνος [ἀσαλής is the one without anxiety]. Aeschylus: "άσαλὴς μανία [carefree madness]." Anecd. Bekk. p. 450, 28. ἀσαλὴς μανία [carefree madness]: ἡ μηδενός φροντίζουσα [the one who thinks about nothing]; σάλη γὰρ ἡ φροντίς [for σάλη is care]. Thus Aeschylus. Hence Nauck thinks that what Photius has at p. 497, 14 is repeated: σάλα: φροντίς [σάλα: care]. Thus Aeschylus: which, with the name of Aeschylus omitted, Suidas explains by φροντίς [care], Hesychius by φροντίς [care] and βλάβη [harm]. Of similar form is the word μάνα [mana], about which Photius p. 246, 4.
carefree: the one without care, the one who thinks about nothing. For σάλη is care. Carefree is the one without anxiety. Aeschylus: "carefree madness"
carefree madness: the one who thinks about nothing; for σάλη is care. Thus Aeschylus
was the title of a tragedy of Aeschylus (fr. 214-218).
Wrongly in the Catalogue of plays Σαλαμίνιοι [Salaminian Men].
Adjective formed for metrical necessity instead of Σαλαμινίαις [Salaminian (dative plural)].
O name most hateful to hear, Salamis.

where the first hand of M has σαλμυδισσία [Salmydissia], which a later hand corrected, as in the apograph it is σαλμυδησσία [Salmydessia] or σαλμυδησία [Salmydesia], and in others too it varies between double and single sigma: see Thes. vol. 7 p. 39. In Sophocles Ant. 967 ὁ Θρηκῶν ἄξενος Σαλμυδησός [the inhospitable Salmydessus of the Thracians], where the codex has Σαλμυδισσός [Salmydissos]. It is the name of a city, a bay, and a shore, ἐπὶ τῆς Θράκης κατὰ τὰ ἀριστερὰ εἰσπλέοντι τὸν Πόντον [on the left as one sails into the Pontus along Thrace], as the scholiast on Apollonius Rhodius says.
the rugged Salmydesian jaw of the sea.
the inhospitable Salmydessus of the Thracians
on the left as one sails into the Pontus along Thrace
The horse, hearing the trumpet's call, rushes eagerly.
The trumpet with its blast set all those things ablaze.
Samos, island of the Aegean Sea.
poetic verb for σώζω [to save], to preserve, keep safe.
σαοί [may he save] for ὀρθοî [may he set upright] is an uncertain conjecture of Hermann at Sept. 229.
where correctly ἀρτάναις [with nooses] is corrected in the Paris apograph, about which I should have noted under the word ἀρτάνη [noose].
I would wish to meet my fate in woven baskets before (thus I wrote for βρόχου [noose]).
He has an old mind, but his flesh is young.
But we, unhonored, with aged flesh.
